conceptual assets.reasoning: The module computes a single combinational decision that enables multiply/divide handling: "valid_cmd <= '1' when (ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu = '1') and (ctrl_i.ir_opcode(5) = '1') and (ctrl_i.ir_funct12(11 downto 5) = \"0000001\") and ((ctrl_i.ir_funct3(2) = '0') or ((ctrl_i.ir_funct3(2) = '1') and DIVISION_EN)) else '0';" The control process tests valid_cmd in S_IDLE to start operations (`if (valid_cmd = '1') then ...`), so integrity of this computed decision determines whether the unit begins an operation. The decision is computed from the input control port.

conceptual assets.concept: Operation start decisions (mul.start and div.start) that capture operands and launch cores
conceptual assets.reasoning: Start signals are computed from valid_cmd and the funct3 opcode bit and directly gate operand capture and core initialization: "mul.start <= '1' when (valid_cmd = '1') and (ctrl_i.ir_funct3(2) = '0') else '0';" and "div.start <= '1' when (valid_cmd = '1') and (ctrl_i.ir_funct3(2) = '1') else '0';". The multiplier process uses mul.start to sample operands (`if (mul.start = '1') then mul.dsp_x <= ...; mul.dsp_y <= ...`), and the divider process uses div.start to initialize quotient/rs2_abs/sign_mod and remainder. Incorrect start signals change whether/when work begins.

conceptual assets.concept: Control FSM state, progress counter and output-enable that govern operation progression and result exposure (ctrl.state, ctrl.cnt, ctrl.out_en)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The clocked control process implements the operation progression: on reset it sets "ctrl.state <= S_IDLE; ctrl.cnt <= (others => '0'); ctrl.out_en <= '0'"; on rising edges it decrements ctrl.cnt in S_BUSY and transitions to S_DONE when "or_reduce_f(ctrl.cnt) = '0' or (ctrl_i.cpu_trap = '1')"; on the DONE->IDLE transition it sets ctrl.out_en <= '1'. These stored fields determine when work runs, completes and when results are exposed; their corruption violates the implemented progress and output gating rules.

conceptual assets.concept: Computed arithmetic result delivered by the unit (res_o) assembled from multiplier or divider outputs
conceptual assets.reasoning: The operation_result process drives the module output when ctrl.out_en = '1': it selects multiplication low/high halves or the divider result: when op_mul_c => res_o <= mul.prod(31 downto 0); when op_mulh* => res_o <= mul.prod(63 downto 32); when others => res_o <= div.res. Thus correctness of mul.prod or div.res and the gating/selection that exposes them is required for the reported result to match the implemented computation.

conceptual assets.concept: Signedness selection for operands (ctrl.rs1_is_signed, ctrl.rs2_is_signed) that control sign-extension and result sign handling
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module derives signedness flags from the opcode: "ctrl.rs1_is_signed <= '1' when (ctrl_i.ir_funct3 = op_mulh_c) or (ctrl_i.ir_funct3 = op_mulhsu_c) or (ctrl_i.ir_funct3 = op_div_c) or (ctrl_i.ir_funct3 = op_rem_c) else '0';" and similar for rs2. These flags are used when sampling/transforming operands (multiplier: mul.dsp_x <= signed((rs1_i(...) and ctrl.rs1_is_signed) & rs1_i) ; divider: tests of rs1_i(...) and ctrl.rs1_is_signed decide quotient sign and rs2_abs). Corruption of these flags changes numeric interpretation and thus result integrity.

conceptual assets.concept: Operand values as consumed/registered by the unit (rs1_i, rs2_i and their registered/normalized forms)
conceptual assets.reasoning: Input operand ports are read and converted into internal forms used by cores: multiplier input registers assign "mul.dsp_x <= signed((rs1_i(rs1_i'left) and ctrl.rs1_is_signed) & rs1_i);" and "mul.dsp_y <= signed((rs2_i(rs2_i'left) and ctrl.rs2_is_signed) & rs2_i);". The divider initializes quotient and rs2_abs from rs1_i/rs2_i on start: e.g. "if (div.start = '1') then if ((rs1_i(rs1_i'left) and ctrl.rs1_is_signed) = '1') then div.quotient <= std_ulogic_vector(0 - unsigned(rs1_i)) else div.quotient <= rs1_i; ... div.rs2_abs <= ...". Integrity of the input ports and these stored, normalized operand values is required for correct arithmetic.
